title: Python/Colab Other-Side Completion Summary

canonical_node.axiom: Runtime artifacts must not support public claims until their status is explicitly bucketed into verified, open/conflicted, simulation-only, empirical-fit, prediction, or utility/support.
definitions: Runtime artifact: a notebook or Python script in the repository.
Claim-status registry: a mapping of public claims to their verification status.
Claim-to-runtime matrix: a mapping of claims to the runtime artifacts that purportedly support them.
Run order: a sequence for executing runtime artifacts.
Data/path ledger: a record of data paths and their references.
Import ledger: a record of imports used by runtime artifacts.
Verified computational result: a result that has been confirmed by execution.
Open/conflicted result: a result that is not yet resolved or has conflicting evidence.
Simulation-only support: support that comes only from simulation, not from formal proof.
Empirical-fit support: support that comes from fitting data.
Prediction support: support that comes from making predictions.
Utility/support only: support that is only for utility or auxiliary purposes.
derivation: The document inventories 25 runtime artifacts and builds registries and ledgers.
The document reports execution readiness phases and claim status counts.
The document identifies claim families and their artifact counts.
The document provides a safe next move via a PowerShell helper.
The document states the main rule: runtime artifacts must not support public claims until status is bucketed.
canonical_node.action: Maintain a claim-status registry and a claim-to-runtime matrix; execute runtime artifacts in phases; ensure every runtime artifact's support for a public claim is classified into one of the six buckets before it is used as evidence.
boundary: Does not execute any runtime artifacts itself.
Does not assign specific claims to specific artifacts in this document.
Does not resolve open or conflicted claims.
test: Check that every runtime artifact has a status bucket assigned before it is cited as support for a public claim.
Check that the claim-status registry is updated after each execution.
Check that the claim-to-runtime matrix is consistent with the registry.
Check that the run order is followed and phases are executed in sequence.

dg1_dependencies: Existing runtime artifacts (20 notebooks, 5 Python scripts)
dg_protocol.dg2_new_capability: Provides a structured inventory and status registry for Python/Colab runtime artifacts, enabling disciplined alignment with Lean evidence standards.
dg_protocol.dg3_preserved_floor: Preserves the requirement that runtime artifacts cannot support public claims without explicit status classification.
dg_protocol.dg4_collapse_if_removed: If this node is removed, runtime artifacts may be used as evidence without status classification, breaking the alignment with Lean evidence discipline.

overstatement_risks: The document does not verify any claims; it only prepares for verification.
The document does not provide evidence that any runtime artifact actually supports a claim.
The document's counts and registries are not themselves verified.
kill_conditions: If runtime artifacts are used to support claims without status bucketing.
If the registries are not maintained or become inconsistent.
If the run order is not followed.
risk.lean_target: The Lean side should provide formal proofs; the Python/Colab side should only provide computational support that is clearly labeled and not conflated with proof.

plain_summary: This document describes the preparation of Python/Colab runtime artifacts for verification, including inventories, registries, and a run plan. It does not verify any claims itself but establishes a discipline: runtime artifacts must be classified into specific support buckets before they can back public claims. The node is coherent and admissible as a procedural guardrail, but it does not establish any mathematical or physical claims.
